clue.text: See 9
Island university is model …

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A remark that some island college is a model, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in the surface only; each clue works alone. UIST is an island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uist is the name of islands in Scotland's Outer Hebrides, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: … fortress to take a look over

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to take a quick look is to peek

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the island's fortress is somewhere to go and look over.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest central tower of a castle, its inner fortress.

clue.text: The very first one to drink in by mouth

indicators.note: in means the drink and the numeral go inside the other piece

parts.note: oral means taken by mouth, as of medicine
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the very first drink they ever took by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the numeral and the drink, which together sit within the word for taken by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something original is the very first of its kind, the one from which copies come.

clue.text: Relative beginners to needlework, in each case expecting

indicators.note: beginners are the starting letters, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A relative is learning needlework while pregnant, as relatives often are in each case.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a relative, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Fuss in cry of kitten in field

indicators.note: in means the fuss is placed inside the kitten's cry

parts.note: a kitten's cry is a mew
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A kitten mewing fussily somewhere in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often one kept for hay.

clue.text: Slip away from the Spanish part of church

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
the apse is the rounded end of a church, usually behind the altar

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks out of the Spanish section of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips away, so the two verbs are synonyms.

parts.note: one's word is one's honour, as in word of honour, so honour's gives word's
worth is value

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of 'Honour's' carries over, so the pieces read as a phrase meaning the value of one's word. WORDSWORTH is the English Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was an English Romantic poet, so the answer is an example of a poet.

clue.text: In which the disappearance of a non-celebrity leads to the poet's transmogrification

definitions.text: In which the disappearance of a non-celebrity leads to the poet's transmogrification

parts.words: In which the disappearance of a non-celebrity leads to the poet's transmogrification
parts.note: describes a verse where an obscure girl dies and the poet is left changed, a Wordsworth stanza about Lucy

explanation.walkthrough: The opening line of the second stanza of Wordsworth's 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways'; the other lines are spread through the grid at the lights marked See 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucy lived unknown, her death is the disappearance, and 'the difference to me' is the poet's transformation.

clue.text: Foreman gives umpire cigarette back

indicators.note: back means the umpire and cigarette, side by side, are read in reverse order letter by letter

parts.note: a referee, or ref, is an umpire
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A foreman hands an umpire a cigarette in return.
explanation.walkthrough: REF then FAG read backwards gives the whole answer. GAFFER is British slang for a boss or foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is a British informal word for a boss, especially a foreman of workers.

clue.text: In truth, rallying is a form of slavery

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A political claim that rallying behind a cause is really a kind of bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall is servitude or bondage, so it is a form of slavery.

clue.text: Bristles edgily

parts.note: reads as reacting irritably, but describes hairs growing at the edges of the face

explanation.definitionFit: Side whiskers are hairs grown down the sides of the face, bristles at its edges.

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'confused' rearranges LANE, ONE and NAG together.

describes something given without anything expected back, as in a relationship where only one side contributes

explanation.definitionFit: A one-way street goes straight forward only, and a one-way arrangement involves no return from the other side.

clue.text: See in the godson an image of oneself

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Seeing one's own reflection in one's godson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word inviting the solver to look in the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self, the picture one holds of oneself.

clue.text: Fabulously dangerous thing to do

parts.note: fabulously means as told in a fable, where mice plan to hang a warning on their predator but none will do it

explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable the mice agree a bell on their enemy would warn them, but nobody dares fit it; the phrase means to undertake a risky task.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take on a perilous job for the common good, from the fable of the mice.

clue.text: Perhaps: "Please do not disturb!"

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be rearranged into a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A sign hung on a hotel door asking not to be disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone sleeping is perhaps the reason for a do-not-disturb sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping guest is the typical reason for a do-not-disturb notice, so the clue as a whole evokes that state.

clue.text: Uncommon tastings pre-pared, got us instead

indicators.note: prepared means made up afresh, so the following letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Unusual tasting sessions were made ready, and we got invited in place of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pre-pared' looks like a trimmed word but is just prepared, the anagram signal, applied to GOT US and INSTEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Degustation is a rare, formal word for tasting, especially of food or wine.

clue.text: Awful f-fino, a losing hazard

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a bad state and need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: A stammered complaint about a dreadful glass of fino sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards an in-off, where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball, is called a losing hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a losing hazard is a stroke where the cue ball is pocketed off another ball, called an in-off.

clue.text: Young person with a soldier each side

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
right and left are the two sides, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: A youngster accompanied by a soldier on both flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left, one letter for each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a female child or young woman, so she is a young person.

clue.text: Hand cream smothering copper? There's an expression!

indicators.note: smothering means the cream covers the metal, so it goes around it

clue.text: Free politician has time on the river

indicators.note: on means the politician and time follow the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician with time off goes free on a river trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; 'has' is a link. The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation; as an adjective it means free from it.

clue.text: You wouldn't want this on your meat or minced fowl, by L__!

definitions.text: You wouldn't want this on your meat

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the single letter L as printed

explanation.surface: A warning about fly-tainted meat, with a mild oath, 'by L__!', as a minced form of Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by L__!' looks like a minced oath, which itself hints at mincing; the letters of FOWL, BY and L are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyblow is the eggs or larvae a fly lays on meat, which nobody wants on their food.
